NBC News, Wed 22 Jul 2026 — Brent crude rose almost 5% to more than $95/bbl for the first time in almost six weeks; WTI up more than 4% to more than $88. Surge as US officials talked down peace-talk prospects after an 11th straight night of strikes and with "two of the world's key supply routes" now disrupted. Houthis said they would impose a maritime blockade on Saudi Arabia; the "Bab el-Mandeb risk picture is deteriorating." US national average petrol +4 cents to $4.06/gal (AAA).
Reuters wire data (via non-approved carriers — for framing only, cite NBC/AJ): Brent session high $95.47, highest since 11 June, settling up ~2-4% ($93-94) into the US afternoon; three-month timespread widened to ~$8.80/bbl (deepest backwardation since 22 May). Analyst Tim Waterer (KCM Trade): "the energy market now has the dual-strait worry." Goldman Sachs (via non-approved carrier): Brent could rally beyond $120 by Q4 if disruption persists — attribute cautiously or omit. Three tankers of Saudi crude for China/India made U-turns in the Red Sea toward Suez.
